newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower after commodities rout.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower after commodities rout.

text.p: COMEX copper reversed its morning's gains to end lower as a wave of selling hit the key metals, grains and energy commodities sectors later in the day.
The red metal market also suffered some jitters because of conflicting expectations over Friday's LME stock report.
"The talk is it's going to be 3,000 to 7,000 tonnes down or maybe 20,000 tonnes will go into warehouses over the course of the next two reporting periods," a broker said.
William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch said copper was largely the victim of a broad based commodities selloff.
"The Commodity Research Bureau index broke very major support at 240 points," O'Neill said. "There was no news in copper."
At 1448 EST the CRB was off 3.75 points at 237.91, off the low of 237.78 points.
December COMEX went out 1.50 cents weaker at 91.30 cents per pound, traded 93.60 to 90.00 cents.
Volume was estimated at 13,000 lots compared to Wednesday's official 14,496 lots.
The financial markets were keenly awaiting a large batch of key U.S. economic data set to be released Friday morning.
